#!/bin/bash
# seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
#
# Makes a worktree that is ready to compile and run Fortress without building anything, by copying the
# build and the caches of a baseline worktree that has been built once, and translating the parts of the
# caches that are keyed by the source tree's absolute path (explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md).
#
#   <base-worktree>  a clean worktree of this repository at some commit B, on which `ant compileAll` and the
#                    library-order recompile (explorations/repo-internals.md, "Compile order matters") have
#                    run, and nothing since.
#   <new-worktree>   where the new worktree goes; made by `git worktree add`, reused if it already exists.
#   <branch>         the branch it checks out: an existing local branch, else origin's, else a new branch
#                    cut from <start-point>, which defaults to B; `-` makes a detached worktree at
#                    <start-point> instead. Old-against-new runs need no copy of the base: tools/old-fortress.sh
#                    runs the base build itself with a private caches folder.
#
# What it does, in order: adds the worktree; copies ProjectFortress/build, ProjectFortress/.dependencies
# and default_repository/caches from the base; renames every file of the AST caches (analyzed_cache,
# interpreter_cache, interpreter_parsed_cache) to the hash of its source's new path (NamingCzar.deCaseName,
# compiler/NamingCzar.java:244-245; GraphNode.java:33 hashes the canonical path) and rewrites the base path
# inside it; rewrites the base path in the bytecode-cache jars' SourceFile attributes (debug information
# only: jars copied unchanged also run, but their stack traces would name the base's files); and makes the
# new worktree the base's replica in its file dates too. The copies keep the base's dates (cp -a), every
# tracked file whose content is the base's takes the base file's date, and every tracked file that differs
# from B, committed or not, is stamped later than everything copied. Dates decide three things. The
# repository uses a cached entry only when it is not older than its source (repository/GraphRepository.java:244,
# :283; a changed api also makes everything that imports it stale, :600-620). Ant regenerates the AST
# nodes, the parsers and Operators.java when an input is newer than the generated file (build.xml:371-384,
# :450-467, :1335-1400); the checkout's own dates make it regenerate them, and javac then recompiles 1,077
# files. And javac recompiles a source newer than its class (build-cache-exploration.md, section 6). So the
# next `fortress compile` of a differing library source rebuilds it, and a worktree whose ProjectFortress/src
# differs from B is seeded with a warning: the copied build is B's, so the worker runs ant compileAll, which
# recompiles the differing sources (and deletes the caches, build.xml:715 and :356), and the library-order
# recompile before its first compiled run. The base's own dates must be a build's: a base built in place by
# ant, or seeded by this script.
#
# A worktree that already has ProjectFortress/build is left alone (a relaunch keeps the worker's own build);
# SEED_FORCE=1 replaces its build and caches with the base's.
#
# Prints one line per step with its time, and the seeded worktree's path last. Exits non-zero, having

(* On the compiled path, a builtinPrimitive body whose string names a static helper of nativeHelpers compiles into a call of that helper, self first for a method. *)
component NativeHelperBindingCompiled
export Executable

less(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT")

trait Shape
  same(self, other:Shape):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
  sameAs(other:Shape, self):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
end

object Box(v:ZZ32) extends Shape
  kind():JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.typeName")
end

add(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intOverflowingAdd")

bazS(s:JavaString):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")
bazI(n:ZZ32):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")

run():() = do
  assert(less(1, 2), "less(1, 2)")
  assert(NOT less(3, 2), "less(3, 2)")
  b = Box(3)
  c = Box(4)
  assert(same(b, b), "same(b, b)")
  assert(NOT same(b, c), "same(b, c)")
  assert(sameAs(b, b), "sameAs(b, b)")
  assert(NOT sameAs(c, b), "sameAs(c, b)")
  assert(b.kind() = "Box", "b.kind()")
  assert(add(2, 3), 5, "add(2, 3)")
  r: ZZ32 := 0
  try
    r := add(2147483647, 1)
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => r := 1
  end
  assert(r, 1, "add(2147483647, 1) raises IntegerOverflow")
  assert(bazS("x".asJavaString) = "baz x", "bazS")
  assert(bazI(7) = "baz 7", "bazI")
  println("PASS")
end

end

(* ZZ32's and Int's operators bound to nativeHelpers keep their values and their IntegerOverflow under walk. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyZZ32Walk
export Executable

overflows(f: () -> ZZ32): Boolean =
  try
    f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
  end

run():() = do
  a: ZZ32 = 2147483647
  b: ZZ32 = -2147483647 - 1
  m: ZZ32 = -1
  assert(3 = 3, true, "=")
  assert(3 = 4, false, "= unequal")
  assert(3 < 4, true, "<")
  assert(4 < 3, false, "< not")
  assert(-a, -2147483647, "unary -")
  assert(overflows(fn () => -b), "unary - of the minimum overflows")
  assert(DOTMINUS b, b, "unary DOTMINUS wraps")
  assert(a - 1 + 1, a, "+")
  assert(overflows(fn () => a + 1), "+ overflows")
  assert(a DOTPLUS 1, b, "DOTPLUS wraps")
  assert(b + 1 - 1, b, "-")
  assert(overflows(fn () => b - 1), "- overflows")
  assert(b DOTMINUS 1, a, "DOTMINUS wraps")
  assert(46340 DOT 46340, 2147395600, "DOT")
  assert(overflows(fn () => 65536 DOT 65536), "DOT overflows")
  assert(7 TIMES 6, 42, "TIMES")
  assert(overflows(fn () => 65536 TIMES 65536), "TIMES overflows")
  assert(7 6, 42, "juxtaposition")
  assert(overflows(fn () => 65536 65536), "juxtaposition overflows")
  assert(65536 DOTTIMES 65536, 0, "DOTTIMES wraps")
  assert(7 DIV 2, 3, "DIV")
  assert((-7) DIV 2, -3, "DIV rounds toward zero")
  assert(overflows(fn () => b DIV m), "DIV of the minimum by -1 overflows")
  assert(12 BITAND 10, 8, "BITAND")
  assert(12 BITOR 10, 14, "BITOR")
  assert(12 BITXOR 10, 6, "BITXOR")
  assert(BITNOT 12, -13, "BITNOT")
  assert(widen(a).asString, "2147483647", "widen")
  assert(unsigned(m).asString, "4294967295", "unsigned")
  assert(a.asString, "2147483647", "asString")
  assert(b.asExprString, "-2147483648", "asExprString")
  assert(asFloat(m), -1.0, "asFloat")
end

end

9:## The disk allowance
10-
11:`df -h /` misleads. Its Size column is the whole disk, about 250 GB, and most of it is reserved and cannot be written. The session may use Used plus Avail, about 37 GB, and Use% is taken of that sum. Read the Avail column: it is what is left.
12-
13-- When the allowance is full, tool output fails with "no space left on device". Check Avail before a long run, and before you seed worktrees or copy builds.
14-- Temporary files that the work never deletes fill it. In this repository, they are mostly the parser's folders in `/tmp`. `fortress-repo`'s `references/build-and-caches.md` gives their sweep.
15-- When it is full, stop your own background processes (`fortress-repo`'s `references/session.md`). Delete what you made and no longer need: scratch, build output, private caches, and finished worktrees whose commits are pushed.
16-- If that is not enough, commit and push, and report that this session's allowance is spent. A new session starts on a fresh machine.
17-
18-## The network
19-
20-Outbound HTTPS goes through the session's proxy, which blocks some hosts. `web.archive.org` resets the connection, and the proxy refuses `labs.oracle.com`.
21-
22-- If you need a research PDF from these hosts, name it in your report. Only the curator can upload it into the session.
23-- To read an archived page that is not a PDF, fetch it through the pure.md reader relay: `https://pure.md/https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>if_/<url>`. The `if_` after the timestamp is required.

add64(a:ZZ64, b:ZZ64):ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedLongArith.unsignedLongOverflowingAdd")

nn32(x:ZZ32):NN32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedIntArith.makeNN32FromZZ32WithSpecialCompilerHackForNN32ResultType")
bits64(x:NN64):ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedLongArith.makeZZ64FromNN64WithSpecialCompilerHackForNN64ArgumentType")
nn64(x:ZZ64):NN64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedLongArith.makeNN64FromZZ64WithSpecialCompilerHackForNN64ResultType")

character(x:ZZ32):Character = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleChar.charMakeCharacterWithSpecialCompilerHackForCharacterResultType")

end

end

facts-extract: part 1 of 1. Its 1 part prints 3272 bytes, about 1500 tokens.
Asked for, and where it is:

== explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, ## Execution model

FACTS.md:26
- F-301 **On the compiled path a native helper is called through a generated wrapper over the box classes, and once the loop is hot C2 inlines the whole path, so the call costs nothing of its own.** A binding `builtinPrimitive("pkg.Class.method")` and a written `import java` alias call compile to the same bytes: an `invokestatic` of `native.pkg.Class.method`, a class the compiled path writes into `nativewrapper_cache/`, which unboxes each argument with `getValue`, calls the helper and boxes its result with `make`, a new box each time (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressMethodAdapter.java:303-327`; `compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32.java:22-24`). A functional method such as `ZZ32`'s `+` reaches the wrapper through the dispatcher, an interface call, the springboard and the trait's static body. C2 inlines all of these frames, the helper, `make` and the box's constructor chain; only C1's profiling code refuses the helper and the chain's deep frames. Escape analysis then removes every temporary box, a helper's result passed into another helper among them, and one box stays per assignment to a mutable variable per iteration: 16 bytes for a `ZZ32`, 24 for an `RR64`. The library's form and the prelude's allocate the same. Observed once on one small program, `perf-probes/helper-calls/HelperCalls.fss`, by `javap`, C2's inlining log and the bytes that JFR counted, with no timing, on a machine shared at a load of 20 to 25; no test checks it. Detail: `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` sections 2 to 5.

FACTS.md:27
- F-302 **In those loops C2 inlines down to depth 12 from the loop, against the 16 at which it stops by default, and a temporary box whose constructor chain passes the limit is no longer removed.** At JDK 25's default `MaxInlineLevel=15` a frame at depth d inlines when d is at most 16. The prelude's `+` reaches `Object.<init>` under its result's box at depth 12, a top-level binding at 10. With the limit lowered to 8, a loop of two nested helper calls rose from 33 to 96 bytes per iteration, since its temporaries' chains no longer inlined. So an operator called from more than 4 further inlined frames keeps its temporary boxes. By reading, the one library's `ZZ32` springboard chain is two classes longer than the prelude's, `ZZ32`, `AnyIntegral`, `Number`, `AnyAdditiveGroup`, `Object`, `Any` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:730`, `:677`, `:380`, `:356`) against `ZZ32`, `Number`, `Object`, `Any` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:210`), since a springboard extends the springboard of its trait's first `extends` entry (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5072-5080`). If `FZZ32` extends the one library's springboard after the switch-over, the margin is 2 frames; not measured, since nothing compiles against the one library yet. Observed once (F-301). Detail: `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` sections 3 and 4.

### The place kept for the hard set

The 109 bindings that cannot name their helper as a bare string (section 4, "The count") are probed now by another worker, whose note is to land as explorations/compile-ladder/plan-24/probes/hard-set.md. This record plans nothing for them. Its rules are those above: two guards per family it moves, an XXX test for each defect it meets, no declaration that another rung changes, and the Appendix I entry left to the gather.

### The rule the rungs keep, and how they meet

- No two rungs change one declaration, and no rung builds on another rung (PLAN, "The principle for the batches"): each rung's tests pass on its own tree. None lands only with another.
- The declarations each rung changes. F: StaticNativeApp.javaFor, Float's 30 strings. Z: ZZ64's 20 strings and ZZ's 16. S: the 8 strings of Long, NN32, BigNum, Char, NN64 and char. K: the two CHOOSE helpers and the two CHOOSE strings.
